sahneler.metin: At twenty four thousand feet, the roof of a jet tore away.
The cabin tore open, and a flight attendant was killed.
So what ripped open a plane?
This jet had flown many short, salty island flights.
Corrosion loosened a joint along a row of rivets.
Tiny fatigue cracks grew, then linked into one long tear.
The pilots still landed it safely on Maui.
Now ageing aircraft are inspected for exactly this damage.

aciklama:
Aloha 243 lost a large section of its roof in flight. The cause: multiple-site fatigue damage and corrosion in a fuselage lap joint.
